name: format-string-101
description:
**format-string-101** -- a small networked service, served as
pwn-as-a-service.

Connect over TCP and you get a fresh process with two live, per-connection
values printed in the banner:

  - the address of a global `auth` cell (stable across connections), and
  - a random 32-bit `nonce` for THIS connection.

Your goal is to make `auth == nonce`. When the service observes that effect it
returns the flag. You get up to 16 input lines per connection.

Because the nonce is regenerated every connection, a replayed payload is
worthless -- you must read the printed values and build your write live.

The downloadable `chall` binary is for offline analysis only. It contains **no
flag**: the per-team flag lives solely in the running service's environment
and is emitted only after the auth check passes. Reading the binary alone will
not give you a flag.

Provided files: `chall` (x86-64 ELF), `chall.c` (source).

Bloqué ? Des indices sont disponibles (ils coûtent quelques points).

Connect:  `nc <host> <port>`

Flag format: `NCTF{...}`

<!-- nctf-connexion -->
> 🔌 Connexion chiffrée : **`ncat --ssl <adresse> 1337`** (pas de `nc` simple) : voir [Se connecter aux instances](/connexion#tcp).
